# contentful_webhook (Resource)

Manages a Contentful Webhook that sends HTTP requests when events match its topics and filters. Configure the receiving endpoint separately.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "contentful_webhook" "this" {
  space_id = var.contentful_space_id

  name = "Example Webhook"
  url  = "https://example.org/webhook"

  active = false

  # Contentful requires at least one topic.
  topics = ["Entry.save", "Entry.publish", "Entry.unpublish"]

  filters = [
    {
      equals = {
        doc   = "sys.environment.sys.id"
        value = "master"
      }
    },
  ]

  http_basic_username    = "webhook"
  http_basic_password_wo = var.webhook_password

  headers = {
    "X-Webhook-Secret" = {
      secret   = true
      value_wo = var.webhook_secret
    },
  }

  transformation = {
    method                 = "POST"
    content_type           = "application/vnd.contentful.management.v1+json"
    include_content_length = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the webhook.
- `space_id` (String) ID of the space containing the webhook. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `topics` (List of String) One or more Contentful event topics, such as `Entry.publish`, `Entry.unpublish`, or `Asset.save`.
- `url` (String) HTTP endpoint that receives events matching the webhook topics and filters. Changing any part of the URL, including its path, sends explicitly supplied write-only header values. Omitted values for retained secret headers and delegated Basic authentication can carry over to the new receiver.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the webhook is active. Defaults to `true`.
- `filters` (Attributes List) Filtering constraints applied after `topics`. Contentful combines filters with logical AND; each filter configures exactly one of `equals`, `in`, `regexp`, or `not`. Null or omitted filters default to the `master` environment; `filters = []` sends no constraints. Supported payload paths and event restrictions are defined by [Contentful webhook filters](https://www.contentful.com/developers/docs/extensibility/webhooks/filters/). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `headers` (Attributes Map) HTTP headers sent by the webhook, keyed by header name. Omitting the map or setting `headers = {}` removes all headers unless `ignore_changes` retains the map or a key. To keep an externally managed header, omit its key and ignore that exact key. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state#secret-custom-headers). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--headers))
- `http_basic_password` (String, Sensitive) HTTP Basic authentication password. Requires a username in the effective plan. Import leaves an omitted password null. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state#webhook-credentials-and-secret-headers) for delegation, refresh and recovery.
- `http_basic_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only alternative to `http_basic_password` for Terraform 1.11.1 or later. Requires a username in the effective plan to set or rotate the password. An ephemeral input keeps the password out of saved plans. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state#basic-authentication).
- `http_basic_username` (String) HTTP Basic authentication username. Supply a password when setting a new username. Retain the same username with both password arguments omitted to preserve an existing password. Removing all Basic credentials from the effective plan clears authentication.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `transformation` (Attributes) Customizes the outgoing webhook HTTP method, Content-Type, Content-Length header, and request body. When omitted, Contentful uses its standard webhook request behavior. Unsupported methods and content types prevent writes, including values retained by ignore_changes. Read and import preserve returned values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transformation))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `space_id/webhook_id` form.
- `version` (Number) The Contentful `sys.version` last observed for this webhook. A possible write-only rotation makes the planned version unknown.
- `webhook_id` (String) System ID of the webhook.

### Nested Schema for `filters`

Optional:

- `equals` (Attributes) Matches when the selected payload property equals the configured value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--equals))
- `in` (Attributes) Matches when the selected payload property equals at least one configured value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--in))
- `not` (Attributes) Inverts exactly one nested `equals`, `in`, or `regexp` filter. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--not))
- `regexp` (Attributes) Matches the selected payload property against a regular-expression pattern. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters--regexp))

<a id="nestedatt--headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `headers`

Optional:

- `secret` (Boolean) Whether Contentful treats the header value as secret. Defaults to `false`. To change the flag under the same name, remove the header in one apply and recreate it in a later apply.
- `value` (String) Supply an initial value or `value_wo` for each configured header when creating or replacing a webhook. Omit both on update to retain an existing secret under its exact name. Ordinary headers require a value. Non-secret values can contain Contentful JSON-pointer templates such as `{ /payload/sys/id }`; secret headers and HTTP Basic credentials are not transformed. Contentful's secret flag does not make the Terraform value sensitive. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state).
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only alternative to `value` for Terraform 1.11.1 or later. Set `secret = true` and supply a randomly generated secret through an ephemeral input. Omit both values to retain an existing secret header. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state#secret-custom-headers).


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.
- `delete` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `read` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `update` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.


<a id="nestedatt--transformation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `transformation`

Optional:

- `body` (String) JSON-encoded custom webhook request body. Use `jsonencode(...)` to construct structured values. When omitted, methods that send a body use Contentful's standard event payload. Contentful can resolve supported JSON-pointer templates and transformation helpers against the original webhook context.
- `content_type` (String) Content-Type for transformed webhook requests. Defaults to `application/vnd.contentful.management.v1+json`; `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` converts the JSON body to form data. See [Contentful transformations](https://www.contentful.com/developers/docs/extensibility/webhooks/transformations/) for supported media types and templates.
- `include_content_length` (Boolean) Whether Contentful includes a `Content-Length` header computed from the transformed request body. Contentful omits the header by default.
- `method` (String) HTTP method for outgoing webhook requests. Contentful defaults to `POST` and supports `POST`, `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE`. `GET` and `DELETE` webhook calls do not include a request body.

## Import

CLI import reads the Webhook into state. An import-block apply can update it immediately. Review the planned receiver URL, topics, filters, transformation and headers before applying. Active defaults to true. Set `active = false` to keep an imported Webhook inactive. Omitting the header map can clear existing headers. [Keeping imported headers](../guides/secrets-and-state#secret-custom-headers)

When applying an import block for a webhook with Basic authentication, keep the existing username in the effective plan and leave both password arguments null to preserve its password. If the username and both passwords are null in the plan, the same apply clears authentication. [Managing imported credentials](../guides/secrets-and-state#basic-authentication)

### By identity (Terraform 1.12 or later)

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    space_id   = var.contentful_space_id
    webhook_id = var.webhook_id
  }
  to = contentful_webhook.this
}
```

### By ID (Terraform 1.5 or later)

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_space_id}/${var.webhook_id}"
  to = contentful_webhook.this
}
```

### From the command line

```shell
terraform import contentful_webhook.this "$CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID/$CONTENTFUL_WEBHOOK_ID"
```
